arguments.new_string:
Verdict: unhealthy. After 45 of the 50 scheduled GRPO steps, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 is still the base model on held-out TACO. `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` (184 problems, n=1, temperature 0.7) is 0.353 at step 0 and 0.348 at step 45, with the ten evals spanning only 0.293–0.364. The same items agree on 159/184 labels between step 0 and step 45 (13 lost, 12 gained). Adjacent evals flip about 15% of labels, which matches sampling noise around a fixed policy, not learning. Held-out pass rate is likewise flat (0.652 at step 0, 0.656 at step 45; one dip to 0.597 at step 10).

Root cause: the actor update is too small to move a 4B policy on this reward inside the fixed 50-step budget. The resolved config (log header, not the shell defaults of 400 steps / eval every 50) is GRPO with AdamW lr 1e-6, `kl_loss_coef` 0.02 (`low_var_kl`, KL in the loss only), `entropy_coeff` 0.001, one PPO epoch, token-mean aggregation, `norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=True`, clip 0.2, batch 16 × 8 samples, mini-batch 16. Token-mean (`agg_loss` in `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`) divides the outcome advantage by the global response-token count. Mean response length is ~1550–1610 tokens, so a group-relative advantage of order 1 is diluted to ~1e-3 per token before the 1e-6 step. With one on-policy epoch, `old_log_prob` is recomputed on the current policy, so the PPO ratio stays ~1.

That scaling shows up in the optimization trace, not only in the formula. `actor/kl_loss` rises from 0 at step 1 to about 0.002 by step 47 (early-10 mean 0.00074, late-10 mean 0.0020), so the KL penalty term is ~4e-5. `actor/pg_clipfrac` and `actor/ppo_kl` are 0 on every logged step. `actor/entropy` goes from an early mean of 0.357 to a late mean of 0.336 (last step 0.270, still in the same band; max over the run is 0.419). `actor/grad_norm` stays finite and nonzero (0.06–0.96, early and late means both ~0.32) and `actor/lr` stays 1e-6, so the optimizer is stepping; the steps do not change behavior. Training binary reward does not rise either: rollout `score`/`acc` is 0.393 on steps 1–10 and 0.391 on steps 40–49 (log `critic/score/mean` early 0.393, late 0.384). Train pass rate actually slips, 0.547 to 0.519.

The binary all-tests-pass reward is a real objective mismatch, and it is not what freezes training. `compute_score` in `verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py` sets `score`/`acc` to 1 only when every test passes; `NaiveRewardManager.run_single` trains on that scalar and drops `pass_rate`. On the held-out set the discarded partial credit is large and stable (pass rate − acc ≈ 0.30; at step 45, 36 of 183 unique prompts score 0 while passing ≥80% of tests). On train it is smaller and more all-or-nothing (discarded mass 0.15 early and 0.13 late; median fail pass rate 0.10 then 0.055). About 51% of the 8-sample train groups contain at least one full pass in both windows, and group score std stays ~0.4–0.47, so GRPO advantages are mostly nonzero. The policy still does not climb the binary reward it is given, nor the denser pass rate.

Symptoms, not causes: the console log stops mid step-48 fail dump (`Training Progress: 48/50`), while rollout files exist through step 49 and metrics through step 47; that is a snapshot cutoff, with no traceback, OOM, or NaN. Response-length clip ratio averages ~1% and peaks at 4.7% against `max_response_length` 16384, and mean length stays ~1.6k tokens, so truncation is not the failure mode. `actor/ppo_kl=0` is the one-epoch on-policy accounting (rollout-vs-actor prob correlation ~0.999), not a skipped update. `use_dynamic_bsz=False` means `ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=16384` is unused; micro-batches are 1 sequence and are not dropped. The disabled critic is expected GRPO. The YAML module name `custom_reward_manager` is not the active manager; the run registers `naive` plus `taco.compute_score`, and train and val dumps use that scorer. The bench baseline swap only replaces GSM8K. `actor.shuffle: False` does not repeat a 16-prompt slice: steps 1–49 use 784 distinct prompts, 16 new ones each step, with zero overlap between the steps checked. Train (1380) and test (184) share no prompts. Test problems have far more cases (median 228 vs train median 11), which helps explain the larger val pass-rate gap, but train binary accuracy is flat on the same objective, so the split shift is not why the policy fails to move. Printed TACO-FAIL lines are a capped sample (115 records, 8 exceptions, 3 timeouts), not an executor outage.
